Descendants of Raana and Mary Roa Walker

Education Grants

Supporting the next generation of our whānau through tertiary education — investing in people as much as in land.

The programme

Investing in our people

The Tutumatai Station Education Grant Programme was established in 2025 to provide financial support to descendants of Raana and Mary Roa Walker who are enrolled in tertiary study. It reflects the Incorporation's belief that investing in whānau is as important as investing in the land.

$1,000
Base grant per year
Available to eligible descendants enrolled full-time in two semesters of accredited tertiary study
$1,200
Maximum (incl. excellence bonus)
10–20% excellence bonus awarded for distinction or high distinction results, assessed by institution's grading scale
70/30
Payment structure
70% upfront on signing acceptance letter. 30% on evidence of successful completion of the academic year

Eligibility & criteria

Who can apply

  • All descendants of the late Raana and Mary Roa Walker are eligible to apply
  • Applicants must be enrolled in a course of tertiary study at a University, Polytechnic, Wānanga, or approved private training establishment
  • The course must lead to a qualification or further opportunity — including trades and apprenticeships
  • Evidence of enrolment or acceptance into the course must be provided
  • Repeat applicants must provide evidence of achievement from the previous year
  • Applicants developing farming and farm management skills are particularly encouraged
  • Grants are awarded at the discretion of the Committee of Management and are subject to available funds

Apply for a grant

Applications open annually. Descendants of Raana and Mary Roa Walker studying in tertiary education are encouraged to apply before 31 March each year.
